title: Weekly cetuximab

agents.name: Cetuximab
agents.mechanism: Blocks growth messages at the cell surface
agents.explanation: Cetuximab attaches to EGFR on the outside of cells and blocks growth messages. In bowel cancer, a validated RAS wild-type result helps identify whether this approach is suitable. In head-and-neck cancer, weekly cetuximab may be combined with radiotherapy under a separate treatment plan. Healthy skin also uses EGFR, so skin and nail effects need early care.
agents.watch: Report rash or sore nails early. Tell the nurse immediately about infusion symptoms. Eye pain, new breathing problems or severe diarrhoea need prompt advice. Blood tests check minerals during treatment and for two months afterwards.
risks: Rash, dry skin, cracks and sore nails
Infusion reaction; rare serious lung or skin effects

questions.a: Cetuximab alone is an option for RAS wild-type bowel cancer that has spread after oxaliplatin and irinotecan have failed, when irinotecan cannot be tolerated. A separate indication combines weekly cetuximab with radiotherapy for locally advanced head-and-neck cancer; the radiation team confirms suitability, including the current NCCP catalogue criteria. Your team explains the aim, alternatives and how benefit will be reviewed.

questions.q: Do I need to enter dates to understand the cycle?
questions.a: No. The graph explains a general pattern. Your hospital arranges appointments; the guide and its safety information are available without entering anything.

questions.q: Will I have a pump at home?
questions.a: There is no home fluorouracil pump in this regimen. Your team chooses a cannula or central line based on your veins and wider treatment plan.

questions.q: What happens if a dose is delayed?
questions.a: The team checks the cause and may delay, reduce, change or stop one medicine. Ask which component changes and when you should next attend; do not restart yourself.

questions.q: How will I know whether it is helping?
questions.a: Scans, symptoms and clinical review assess benefit. A rash, side effect or good day alone cannot show whether the cancer is responding.

For the head-and-neck indication, cetuximab starts one week before radiation and continues weekly alongside it. The graphic below shows the relationship. Colorectal cetuximab alone does not include a routine radiation course.

questions.q: What about fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding?
questions.a: Discuss fertility preservation and reproductive plans before treatment. Ask for the contraception and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine; the whole regimen may require longer precautions than one medicine alone.
RAS testing selects cetuximab treatment in colorectal cancer. It is not the selection test for the separate head-and-neck radiotherapy indication. Confirm the cancer-specific plan with your team.

questions.q: Which checks continue when treatment changes or finishes?
questions.a: Monthly electrolytes, magnesium and calcium for two months after the last cetuximab dose; assign responsibility before treatment ends. Response assessment follows the consultant plan; head/neck radiation follow-up is coordinated separately.

phases_note: This is a general explanation, not an appointment calendar. Delays or changes are decided by your team. Each medicine can need a different change.
timeline_note: NCCP defines the treatment days. Symptom bands are broad educational guidance; reactions can occur on any day, and cumulative effects may continue between cycles.
safety_note: Fever, shivers or suddenly feeling unwell require immediate contact. Serious symptoms override any timeline or diary.
teachback: Can you explain which visits are planned, whether a pump is involved, and which symptoms mean you should call today? No dates or symptom scores are needed to use this guide.
consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, expected benefit, serious and lasting risks, fertility/pregnancy precautions and the contact plan. Confirm RAS selection for colorectal treatment, infusion premedication, skin care and post-treatment mineral checks. Explain the separate radiotherapy indication and swallowing/skin support.
urgent_extra: New breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink require prompt assessment. Report eye pain, blurred vision, blistering or infected skin promptly.

chapters.title: Your treatment aim
chapters.intro: The setting changes what benefit means.

items.title: Why this option?
items.text: Cetuximab alone is an option for RAS wild-type bowel cancer that has spread after oxaliplatin and irinotecan have failed, when irinotecan cannot be tolerated. A separate indication combines weekly cetuximab with radiotherapy for locally advanced head-and-neck cancer; the radiation team confirms suitability, including the current NCCP catalogue criteria. Your team explains the aim, alternatives and how benefit will be reviewed.

items.title: A plan that can change
items.text: Ask whether the aim is to reduce recurrence risk, control cancer, relieve symptoms or support a local treatment. Your preferences and priorities matter.

items.title: Separate head-and-neck evidence
items.text: A randomised trial compared radiotherapy plus weekly cetuximab with radiotherapy alone and found improved local control and survival. It did not compare cetuximab with cisplatin; it cannot establish that cetuximab is equivalent to cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy.

items.title: Blood tests and medicines
items.text: Review blood counts, kidney/liver tests, symptoms, allergies and all medicines and supplements.  Tell the team about red-meat allergy or tick bites before cetuximab because these can be associated with infusion-reaction risk.

items.title: Preparing access
items.text: Allow for blood tests, review, pharmacy preparation, infusion and observation. A port is not automatically required; ask which access is suitable.

chapters.title: Symptoms in context
chapters.intro: Report what changed and how it affects you.

items.title: When to call
items.text: New breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse, severe diarrhoea or inability to drink require prompt assessment. Report eye pain, blurred vision, blistering or infected skin promptly.

items.title: Bowel symptoms
items.text: Follow your written rescue plan. Fever, blood, severe pain, reduced urine or inability to drink needs urgent advice.

items.title: Skin or nerve changes
items.text: Start the prescribed skin-care plan early, use moisturiser and sun protection, and report painful or infected skin or nails. Keep mineral blood-test appointments during treatment and for two months after cetuximab.

items.title: Food, activity and practical help
items.text: Use prescribed anti-sickness medicines, pace activities and ask for nutritional, emotional or practical support.

items.title: Pregnancy and fertility
items.text: Discuss fertility preservation and reproductive plans before treatment. Ask for the contraception and breastfeeding instructions for every medicine; the whole regimen may require longer precautions than one medicine alone.

chapters.title: Visits and treatment sequence
chapters.intro: Know which steps happen in the clinic and at home.

items.title: The exact delivery plan
items.text: Cetuximab on Day 1. No home chemotherapy pump. A repeating 7-day cycle. The number of cycles depends on benefit, side effects and your treatment plan. For head-and-neck radiotherapy: start cetuximab one week before radiation, then continue weekly during radiation until it ends.

items.title: Radiotherapy relationship
items.text: For the head-and-neck indication, cetuximab starts one week before radiation and continues weekly alongside it. The graphic below shows the relationship. Colorectal cetuximab alone does not include a routine radiation course.

items.title: Head-and-neck radiation support
items.text: Ask the radiation team about dental review, mouth care, pain relief, nutrition and swallowing support. Radiation-related mouth/throat soreness and skin changes can build during the course and continue afterwards. Trouble swallowing fluids or worsening breathing needs urgent assessment.

items.title: Symptoms and monitoring
items.text: Continue the cetuximab skin plan and mineral checks for two months after the last dose. Ask which medicines to continue, when to seek help and how response will be assessed.

items.title: Next decisions
items.text: The team reviews benefit, side effects and your priorities. Supportive and palliative care can help alongside active treatment. Ask for a clear next-step and contact plan.

purpose: For selected bowel cancer that has spread, cetuximab aims to control the cancer after previous treatments. For selected locally advanced head-and-neck cancer when platinum chemotherapy is unsuitable, it is combined with radiotherapy. Your team confirms which pathway applies.
schedule_summary: One larger first infusion is followed by weekly infusions. Bowel-cancer treatment continues while helping and tolerated. For head-and-neck treatment, cetuximab starts one week before radiotherapy and continues until radiation treatment finishes.
context_label: Selected metastatic colorectal cancer; or locally advanced head/neck cancer with radiotherapy when platinum is unsuitable

day_groups.title: Treatment and checks
day_groups.body: The team reviews blood tests, symptoms and your prescription before treatment. Premedicines and observation are part of cetuximab visits.
day_groups.action: Know the contact number and the next planned visit.

day_groups.title: Care between visits
day_groups.body: Follow the skin-care or bowel-symptom plan provided. There is no pump to remove.
day_groups.action: Call early for symptoms; do not wait for the next appointment.

day_groups.title: Recovery and the next review
day_groups.body: The team uses symptoms, tests and your priorities to decide what happens next.
day_groups.action: Bring questions and a symptom record if useful; this is optional.

support.title: First cetuximab dose
support.text: Skin care and sun protection under local EGFR policy. First two doses require post-infusion observation; delayed-reaction education. Monthly electrolytes/Mg/Ca for two months after last dose.

support.title: Subsequent weekly cetuximab
support.text: Premedication continues for subsequent infusions. Head/neck RT requires separate mucosal, skin, swallow and nutrition support. Post-treatment monthly electrolytes/Mg/Ca for two months.

evidence.title: Why this treatment is offered
evidence.intro: In selected previously treated bowel cancer, cetuximab improved disease control and survival compared with supportive care. Separate head-and-neck evidence supports adding it to radiotherapy in the appropriate setting.
evidence.interpretation: In selected previously treated bowel cancer, cetuximab improved disease control and survival compared with supportive care. Separate head-and-neck evidence supports adding it to radiotherapy in the appropriate setting.
evidence.population: Previously treated KRAS wild-type metastatic CRC; separate locally advanced squamous head/neck population.
evidence.limitations: CO.17 used older KRAS testing. Head/neck evidence is separate and does not establish equivalence to platinum chemoradiation.

chronology_notes.title: Your planned visits
chronology_notes.text: Cetuximab on Day 1. No home chemotherapy pump. A repeating 7-day cycle. The number of cycles depends on benefit, side effects and your treatment plan. For head-and-neck radiotherapy: start cetuximab one week before radiation, then continue weekly during radiation until it ends.

chronology_notes.title: No guaranteed safe days
chronology_notes.text: An infection, reaction or other urgent problem can occur at any time. The graph does not predict a personal low point.

chronology_notes.title: Care continues
chronology_notes.text: Continue the skin-care plan and mineral checks arranged after cetuximab. Ask which medicines to continue and when your next review is planned.

Tests check magnesium and other minerals even when you feel well.

Tell the nurse immediately about itching, swelling or flushing.
Diarrhoea, increased stoma output or dehydration: call early.
Report painful rash, cracks or infected skin early.
Fever, shivers or sudden illness: contact oncology immediately.
Pain, swelling, leakage or a loose connection needs immediate advice.

steps.title: Before treatment
steps.text: Confirm tests, medicines and the exact schedule.

steps.title: Prepare for the visit
steps.text: Arrange transport if premedicines or symptoms affect driving.

steps.title: At the day ward
steps.text: Blood results, symptoms and venous access are checked.

steps.title: Infusion and observation
steps.text: Weekly cetuximab: first infusion about two hours, later doses often one hour. Fortnightly cetuximab: about two hours. Premedicines, review and observation add time.

steps.title: At home
steps.text: Follow the skin-care and/or bowel plan. There is no pump to disconnect.

steps.title: Next review
steps.text: Confirm the next appointment and follow-up tests.

details.title: Do I need a port?
details.text: A peripheral cannula or existing central line may be used. A port is not automatically needed; the team considers your veins and overall treatment plan.

details.title: If the schedule changes
details.text: Ask the unit to confirm the next visit and which medicine is being changed. Do not copy dates from another regimen.

sections.title: Treatment phases and appointments
sections.text: One larger first infusion is followed by weekly infusions. Bowel-cancer treatment continues while helping and tolerated. For head-and-neck treatment, cetuximab starts one week before radiotherapy and continues until radiation treatment finishes.

sections.title: Checks after treatment
sections.text: Monthly electrolytes, magnesium and calcium for two months after the last cetuximab dose; assign responsibility before treatment ends. Response assessment follows the consultant plan; head/neck radiation follow-up is coordinated separately.

sections.title: Access and practical support
sections.text: Day-unit IV access; no home fluorouracil pump. Head/neck pathway requires a separate radiation appointment and nutrition/swallowing support plan.

indication_text: Selected metastatic colorectal cancer; or locally advanced head/neck cancer with radiotherapy when platinum is unsuitable
administration_text: The first infusion usually takes two hours and later infusions one hour. Extra observation is needed after the first two infusions. There is no home chemotherapy pump.
monitoring_summary: FBC, renal and liver profile; adequate marrow and organ function; ECOG 0–3. Confirm indication: EGFR-expressing RAS wild-type mCRC with the exact prior-treatment conditions; or locally advanced squamous head/neck cancer with RT and platinum ineligibility. Ask about previous antibody infusion reactions, red-meat allergy, tick bites and anti-cetuximab IgE results. Regular FBC, renal and liver profile; review skin, nails, eyes, respiratory symptoms, hydration and electrolyte abnormalities. Vital signs before, at one hour and after infusion; one-hour observation after doses 1 and 2. After two tolerated doses the source permits stopping that observation/vital-sign schedule. Monthly electrolytes, magnesium and calcium for two months after the last cetuximab dose; assign responsibility before treatment ends. Response assessment follows the consultant plan; head/neck radiation follow-up is coordinated separately.
